lessons.title: Prompt injection & trust boundaries
lessons.description: Threat-model retrieval, models, tools and agents.
lessons.conceptOverview: Direct and indirect prompt injection attempt to turn untrusted input into instructions. Retrieved documents and tool results remain data even when they contain imperative text. Validate proposed actions against authenticated user intent outside the model. Tool poisoning and malicious MCP descriptions can target tool selection and arguments.

lessons.title: Least privilege & supply-chain defense
lessons.description: Threat-model retrieval, models, tools and agents.
lessons.conceptOverview: Scope credentials and tool capabilities per task. Use sandboxing, egress controls and output validation; never expose secrets to unnecessary model context. Model supply chains include weights, executable loaders and dependencies. Unsafe deserialization can execute code, so prefer constrained formats and verified provenance.

lessons.title: Red teaming & security evaluation
lessons.description: Threat-model retrieval, models, tools and agents.
lessons.conceptOverview: Test exfiltration, RAG poisoning, privilege escalation, malicious tool outputs and tenant isolation. Map cases to a risk framework such as OWASP, but use the current framework version for a real assessment. Record exploit preconditions, impact and regression cases. Separate prevented actions from merely refused text.
